selected_evidence.requirement: datauser account exists and 100MB filesystem-enforced quota configured under /srv/data
selected_evidence.summary: Initial state showed no datauser/no /srv/data mount; second command created datauser, built dedicated XFS loop mount at /srv/data, and set xfs_quota user limit bsoft=bhard=100m for datauser

selected_evidence.requirement: Quota is enforced by the filesystem itself (kernel-level), not a soft/script check
selected_evidence.summary: dd write of 150MB as datauser was cut off by the kernel at exactly 100M with 'Disk quota exceeded'; a 10MB write succeeded and quota report reflected usage
Captured boot_id 06339ff3-9f53-4e1d-9bf4-1210144ee001, confirmed /srv/data mounted with usrquota,prjquota, quota report showing datauser at 10M/100M, and smallfile present
systemctl reboot issued in background; command returned 'reboot issued' successfully before the node disconnected

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity, not just elapsed time
selected_evidence.summary: Connection timed out/reset during reboot window, then exec succeeded again returning new boot_id 964e471a-aab6-4428-8b06-3676123a3533, differing from baseline, with uptime reset to 0 minutes

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data and re-verified quota enforcement
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data remained mounted with usrquota,prjquota options, quota config and prior data (smallfile) intact, and a repeat 150MB write as datauser again failed at exactly 100MB with Disk quota exceeded

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail

echo "=== STEP 1: create datauser ==="
if ! id datauser >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo -n useradd -m -d /home/datauser -s /bin/bash datauser
fi
id datauser

echo "=== STEP 2: create backing image for /srv/data ==="
sudo -n mkdir -p /srv/data
sudo -n mkdir -p /var/lib/srv-data
IMG=/var/lib/srv-data/srv-data.img
if [ ! -f "$IMG" ]; then
  sudo -n fallocate -l 1024M "$IMG" || sudo -n dd if=/dev/zero of="$IMG" bs=1M count=1024
fi
sudo -n mkfs.xfs -f "$IMG"

echo "=== STEP 3: fstab entry ==="
sudo -n cp -a /etc/fstab /etc/fstab.bak.disk-quota
if ! grep -q "$IMG" /etc/fstab; then
  echo "$IMG /srv/data xfs loop,uquota,prjquota 0 0" | sudo -n tee -a /etc/fstab
fi
cat /etc/fstab | grep srv-data

echo "=== STEP 4: mount ==="
mountpoint -q /srv/data && sudo -n umount /srv/data || true
sudo -n mount /srv/data
findmnt /srv/data

echo "=== STEP 5: ownership ==="
sudo -n chown datauser:datauser /srv/data
sudo -n chmod 750 /srv/data
ls -ld /srv/data

echo "=== STEP 6: set 100MB user quota for datauser ==="
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'limit -u bsoft=100m bhard=100m datauser' /srv/data
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'report -u -h' /srv/data

echo "=== STEP 7: verify enforcement (write >100MB as datauser) ==="
set +e
sudo -n -u datauser dd if=/dev/zero of=/srv/data/testfile bs=1M count=150 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e
echo "dd exit code (expect nonzero due to quota): $RC"
ls -lh /srv/data/testfile
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'report -u -h' /srv/data

echo "=== STEP 8: cleanup test file, verify small write still works ==="
sudo -n rm -f /srv/data/testfile
sudo -n -u datauser dd if=/dev/zero of=/srv/data/smallfile bs=1M count=10
ls -lh /srv/data/smallfile
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'report -u -h' /srv/data
echo "=== DONE ==="
